data.name: ESign.Help.Mine
data.value: My Signature is where you keep the signature sample you may attach to an electronic signature and see the signatures you have given; it needs the esign.my-samples.manage key. Saving a sample asks for your password again. When the company policy requires approval, a new sample stays Pending until another person with esign.samples.approve approves it, and you can never approve your own sample (four eyes). You have one active sample at a time; a sample already used in a signature cannot be withdrawn, only deactivated.

data.name: ESign.Help.Requests
data.value: My Signature Requests lists the work a module is waiting for you to sign; it needs the esign.requests.read key. The list is ordered by due date, the nearest first, and on the same due date the newer request comes first. Signing uses the meaning named in the request and asks for your password; rejecting needs a reason of at least ten characters, and the requester is informed.

data.name: ESign.Help.Verify
data.value: Signature Verification shows the signatures on a record and their state today: valid, record changed, tampered or invalidated; it needs the esign.signatures.read key. Verifying (esign.signatures.verify) compares what was signed with the record as it is now, and the signature record itself never changes. Invalidating a signature needs esign.signatures.invalidate, your password and a reason of at least ten characters, and is stored as a separate entry. Company records are shown only for the companies in your data scope; your own signatures are always shown.

data.name: ESign.Help.Export
data.value: Audit Export lets you filter signature records and download them as PDF or CSV for audits and inspections; it needs the esign.signatures.export key. Every export gets a number, and who exported, with which filter, how many records and the SHA-256 hash of the file are recorded and cannot be changed. Dates are printed in UTC, and company records are limited to your data scope.

data.name: ESign.Help.Policy
data.value: Signature Policy decides which action requires an electronic signature, its default meaning and the visual signature rule; reading needs esign.policy.read and changing needs esign.policy.manage. It also sets whether the password is asked at every signature or once within a validity window, and whether a new signature sample must be approved before use. A company can have rows that differ from the tenant policy and can revert them; every change needs a reason and is written to the history below.

data.name: ESign.Help.Meanings
data.value: Signature Meanings define what a signature declares, for example I approve or I reviewed; the signing dialog offers this list. Reading needs esign.meanings.read and managing needs esign.meanings.manage. The code of a meaning is permanent and never changes; its display name is entered per language, and the text in the signer language at the moment of signing is stored in the signature record. A meaning that is no longer used is deactivated, not deleted, and cannot be chosen for new signatures.

data.name: ESign.Help.Approvals
data.value: Signature Sample Approvals is where new signature samples are reviewed when the company policy requires approval; approving needs esign.samples.approve and rejecting needs esign.samples.reject. Under the four-eyes rule no decision button is drawn for your own sample. A rejection needs a reason, and every decision is written to the decision log below and cannot be changed. An approved sample becomes the only active sample of its owner.
